label: rem:poincare-sphere-ohtsuki-slope-prior-art
title: Prior art: the Ohtsuki series of $\Sigma(2,3,5)$ grows like $(30/\pi^2)^n\,n!$
html:
Jacoby and Lawrence define the slope of a rational homology sphere M as \sigma(M) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \lambda_n(M)/(n\,\lambda_{n-1}(M)), where \lambda_n are the coefficients of its Ohtsuki series, and record from Lawrence–Rozansky that for a Seifert-fibred manifold the slope exists and equals \sigma = \pm \prod_i P_i/\pi^2 [jacoby-lawrence2004, \S 4.3, p. 65]. For an integer homology sphere \pi^2\sigma \in \mathbb{Z}. They also note that the WRT invariants of the mirror image satisfy Z_K(\bar M)(q) = Z_K(M)(q^{-1}) at all roots of unity, so the Ohtsuki series of \bar M is obtained by q \mapsto q^{-1} [jacoby-lawrence2004, \S 4.2, p. 64].

For the Poincaré homology sphere \Sigma(2,3,5), the Seifert fibration over the S^2(2,3,5) orbifold in the icosahedral bridge, this gives |\pi^2\sigma| = 2\cdot 3\cdot 5 = 30: the coefficients grow like (30/\pi^2)^n\, n!, so the series in h has zero radius of convergence and any value away from h = 0 needs a resummation. The number 30 is also the Coxeter number of E_8, but the paper does not mention E_8, and the agreement is not shown to be more than the arithmetic 2\cdot 3\cdot 5. The mirror rule is the q \mapsto q^{-1} bar involution stated for a 3-manifold invariant; it says nothing about the value of the series at the real substrate point.
